newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Grain-Australia nears bumper crop.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Grain-Australia nears bumper crop.

text.p: With expectations of a record or near-record wheat harvest in Australia this year, further underscored with the Australian Wheat Board lifting its crop estimate, trading in wheat futures was subdued last week.
Price gains in the most active January contract at the Sydney Futures Exchange turned into profit-taking losses later in the week
Trading ended the week with January down 50 cents at A$163 a tonne.

The AWB put the 1996/97 crop at 21.5 million tonnes. This compares with 21.3 million tonnes estimated by the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) and 21.28 million by Australia Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd.

Physical activity was more dynamic than the futures market, with the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) confirming to Reuters on Friday the sale of 250,000 tonnes of wheat for January-February delivery to Iraq.
The AWB said the sale was worth A$60 million.
The sale was made under the United Nations food for oil agreement with Iraq.
AWB spokesman Alec Nicol said the deal renews ties between Australia and Iraq, which became subdued after the Gulf War.
Nicol said Australia now aims to sell Iraq on average about 100,000 tonnes of wheat a month.
Local grains traders in Australia disputed some suggestions the wheat fetched in excess of A$200 a tonne.
"That would be nice, but a bit high," one said.

The AWB said pool deliveries of the 1996/97 wheat harvest had now passed the 12.5 million tonne mark with quality continuing to be good in most parts although there were isolated reports of very low protein deliveries from some very heavy
crops.
Cash bids for milling grades firmed by around A$4 a tonne last week in most areas except Victoria where prices dropped A$4 a tonne under harvest pressure, it said in its weekly report.
Meanwhile, Australia is seen vying for part of a potential feed barley tender for Saudi Arabia.
Trade sources said, however, that some Australian growers may be holding back feed barley in the hopes of blending or otherwise upgrading the feed barely in order to fetch a higher price premium.
But with a strengthening in feed barley prices last week, more farmers could be encouraged to part with material, traders said.
The Australian Barley Board last week lifted its estimated 1996/97 season gross pool return by A$5 a tonne to A$152 a tonne in Victoria state and to A$147 a tonne in South Australia.
However, the gross pool return estimate for malting barley remained unchanged at A$210 a tonne.
The ABB expects to export 400,000 tonnes of barley by the end of December and more than 200,000 tonnes in January.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 973-1800
